Remember the endosymbiotic idea, mitochondria and chloroplasts keep their own $70S$ ribosomes and circular DNA like prokaryotes, but only the organelles have a double envelope.
walkthrough:
**Read the three circles**

Think of each circle as a checklist. Top left means has ribosomes smaller than $80S$ (that is $70S$). Top right means has circular DNA. Bottom means is surrounded by a double membrane.

Region B is where the top two overlap but outside the bottom circle.

**Check prokaryotes, mitochondria and chloroplasts**

All three have $70S$ ribosomes, which are smaller than the $80S$ ribosomes of eukaryotes. All three also have circular DNA with no histones.

Only mitochondria and chloroplasts are surrounded by a double membrane. A prokaryotic cell has a single plasma membrane (plus wall or capsule), not a double envelope.

**Pick the shared region**

The features shared by all three must be $70S$ ribosomes plus circular DNA, but NOT double membrane. That is exactly region B, the overlap of the top two circles only.

options.A: Region A is ribosomes smaller than $80S$ only, without circular DNA. All three also have circular DNA, so this is incomplete.
options.B: Region B is $70S$ ribosomes plus circular DNA but no double membrane. This fits prokaryotes, mitochondria and chloroplasts perfectly.
options.C: Region C is circular DNA only, without small ribosomes. All three also have $70S$ ribosomes, so this is incomplete.
options.D: Region D adds a double membrane to the other two features. Prokaryotes are not surrounded by a double membrane, so D only fits the two organelles.
